organization: Rainbow Community Center of Contra Costa County
program: Finite psychotherapy access within a broad LGBTQ community organization

nutshell.headline: Real clinical services, but weakly measured throughput and limited ordinary-gift evidence
nutshell.body: The research list uses the central scenario: $38,725,116 per 10 Bay QALYs. Signed subjective mixture: $8,105,143 per 10 Bay QALYs. Central scenario: $38,725,116. This charges the whole organization but quantifies only finite psychotherapy health, not complete expected value.
nutshell.whyItMayWork: Affirming therapy can improve symptoms for people who otherwise lack suitable care. Trainee-supported clinical delivery is an actual service, not merely outreach reach.
nutshell.whyWeAreCautious: The favorable 10% scenario supplies 97.75% of signed expected benefit. Annual completed courses, current capacity and incremental private funding response are unknown.
nutshell.recommendationBlocker: HOLD giving recommendation. The central and weighted therapy-only estimates are above $1M per 10 Bay QALYs, and no priced marginal clinical capacity is verified.

programSection.body: Rainbow provides mental-health counseling, youth/senior groups, community support, case management and sexual-health testing/navigation in Contra Costa County. Its detailed sexual-health page describes PrEP navigation and treatment referrals to public clinics. These are not verified treatment starts. The organization explicitly says it is not a crisis center.

steps.title: Estimate actual therapy delivery
steps.detail: Use a small clinician-capacity prior anchored only loosely to the six-name trainee roster; convert attended sessions into course starters, then meaningful completed person-condition courses.

steps.title: Credit finite symptom change
steps.detail: Apply a bounded utility-duration proxy, adjusted for local treatment differences and realistic alternative care; no suicides or HIV infections automatically prevented.

steps.title: Retain whole-gift scope
steps.detail: All costs remain, while unquantified community, housing and sexual-health pathways remain unknown—not zero. Cash response reflects existing public-funded baseline.

programSection.boundary: Only psychotherapy symptom health is quantified. Peer support, senior/youth community services, housing navigation and HIV/STI linkage may matter but lack a nonoverlapping completed-care denominator here. They are not assigned zero benefit. No program-only cost substitution, free donated labor assumption, lifetime suicide-prevention award or referral-to-treatment shortcut.

model.headline: $8,105,143 per 10 Bay QALYs
model.body: Weighted annual Bay health is 1.57100132; a bounded $10,000 gift produces 0.012337845583078553. Central modeled completed unique courses are 100.8, not an observed count.

equation.label: Signed finite therapy health
equation.expression: gift / whole expense × funding × Bay share × [unique course starters × completion × utility gain × duration × local transfer × clinical access increment − unique starters × harm]

inputs.label: Whole annual expense
inputs.basis: All programs and overhead retained. $1,110 depreciation and other noncash accounting entries not removed without reconciliation; not a complete economic-resource price.

inputs.label: Annual clinician equivalents
inputs.basis: Six names on an undated trainee roster anchor only approximate scale. Five is not five observed FTE; eight allows other providers. Turnover and actual clinical hours unknown.

inputs.label: Attended sessions per clinician-week
inputs.basis: Judgment, not a published caseload; excludes no-show appointments by definition.

inputs.label: Clinical weeks per year
inputs.basis: Judgment for trainee calendar/leave; no annual throughput reported.

inputs.label: Average consumed sessions per course starter
inputs.basis: Includes partial courses; not ten sessions observed per client. Trial protocols do not establish local delivery.

inputs.label: Meaningful-course completion fraction
inputs.basis: Judgment applied to benefit only. No trial intention-to-treat estimate is multiplied by completion.

inputs.label: Distinct person-condition course fraction
inputs.basis: Avoids treating repeat courses or couple/family encounters as additional clinical people. No multiple diagnoses added.

inputs.label: Conditional symptom utility gain
inputs.basis: Preference-based value is an analyst proxy, not symptom-score conversion or LGBTQ identity value.

inputs.label: Finite benefit duration
inputs.basis: Integrated short-term symptom benefit, not mortality or lifetime identity-related gain. Flat duration is a simplifying assumption.

inputs.label: Local modality/population transfer
inputs.basis: Roster includes narrative/somatic approaches, not proven trial-protocol CBT. Trial populations are narrower than all ages/genders served.

inputs.label: Benefit beyond alternative care
inputs.basis: Conditional on service delivered; other counseling/covered services may substitute. Not a second attendance discount.

inputs.label: Additional service from ordinary cash
inputs.basis: Cash response beyond already financed public/private baseline; separate from clinical alternatives. Not proven funding room.

inputs.label: Bay benefit share
inputs.basis: Contra Costa footprint, not verified patient residences. Same fraction applied to harms.

inputs.label: Independent burden per unique starter
inputs.basis: Judgment for burdens/adverse experiences beyond clinical change; applies even to non-completers.

inputs.label: Joint subjective scenario weights
inputs.basis: Locked before first output, not empirically calibrated. No coefficient retuning.

model.uncertaintyBoundary: No observed annual clinical-course denominator. The six-name roster is not six full-time providers. Clinical response is a conditional analyst utility-duration proxy; it is NOT an imported intention-to-treat coefficient with a second completion penalty. Completion controls clinically meaningful course delivery; unique fraction controls repeated person-condition counting; transfer controls modality/population; access controls alternate care; funding controls cash-created delivery. These separate concepts remain empirically uncertain and correlated. Favorable-world removal raises price sharply. Subjective mass below $1M is 0.1 and below $100k is 0; these are not calibrated probabilities.
model.fundingBoundary: FY2025 expense $1,273,319 versus prior $1,752,448. Government contributions $1,232,945 of $1,494,629 revenue (~82.5%); fees $78,930. Net assets $454,076, liabilities $351,672 and surplus $221,310 do not prove cash room or lack of need. Annual clinical throughput and allocation of public contracts are unknown. Fee revenue is not all therapy revenue. The $10,609 MSW intern stipend line does not price full therapy delivery or donated supervision. All overhead retained; donated resources/partners unpriced. No donation link offered because destination/payment verification failed despite official site navigation link.

evidence.result: Expense $1,273,319; government revenue $1,232,945; broad program narrative with no annual completed-care count.
evidence.transfer: Retain whole expense. Pandemic-era text is not proof of current service volumes; food Supply Train is explicitly described as ended August 2023.

evidence.design: Current undated official service and intern pages
evidence.population: All-age clinical services and six listed trainees
evidence.result: Individual, couples, family and adolescent therapy; several narrative/somatic modalities.
evidence.transfer: Roster is not FTE or courses; modeled capacity and completion are judgments. Do not assume standardized CBT or add family members automatically.

evidence.design: 2015 randomized immediate treatment versus three-month waitlist
evidence.population: 63 young gay/bisexual men, New York City, symptomatic and not in regular care
evidence.result: Affirmative CBT pilot reported symptom and behavioral improvements.
evidence.transfer: Small narrow waitlist study; no QALY coefficient or Rainbow treatment-fidelity evidence. Do not generalize to all identities, ages, conditions or modalities.

evidence.population: 254 young sexual-minority men; ESTEEM versus HIV counseling/testing or affirmative community counseling
evidence.result: Primary sexual-risk outcome not significantly better; secondary mental-health comparisons did not reach significance after false-discovery correction.
evidence.transfer: Small-to-moderate nonsignificant advantages do not prove zero benefit, but sharply weaken claims of large added value over existing appropriate care. Supports clinical-null and alternative-care uncertainty.

evidence.design: 2018 trial-based economic evaluation of CBT plus usual care versus usual care
evidence.population: 212 adolescents with depression who declined/stopped antidepressants
evidence.result: Reported 26.8 extra depression-free days and .067 QALYs over 12 months. Simple stated .4 decrement ×26.8/365 gives .02937; reconciliation unresolved.
evidence.transfer: Neither figure is directly imported. Rainbow's central .06 ×.5 ×.65 = .0195 conditional Q per completed course is a judgment; youth CBT evidence does not validate local adult/family care.

evidence.result: PrEP information/referrals and treatment connections; public clinic schedules and payer access listed.
evidence.transfer: No retained PrEP, ART or STI-treatment outcomes counted; broad clinical page wording must not override the detailed referral boundary.

reservations: Whole-cost partial-health price is not complete organization value; important unquantified pathways could change it.
No annual unique course denominator or observed symptom utility; roster-based capacity is weak.
Public funding dominates reported revenue; current private cash-created capacity is unknown.
The favorable 10% world drives nearly all signed expected benefit.
Trial methods/populations differ from local narrative/somatic, couples and family care.
Official site says not a crisis center; no suicide mortality credit.
excludedBenefits: HIV infections averted or ART retention inferred from testing/referrals
Suicide deaths averted or lifetime survival from routine counseling
Peer-group and family-member benefits added without deduplication
Current food-pantry benefit from discontinued Supply Train
Housing, social support, youth/senior wellbeing and dignity—unquantified, not zero
